question: Related Questions Q. Talaq 2432 views Q. I was in nikkah with my husband but rukhsati had not taken place. 12019 views Q. This is to help me for a reason, i recently got married and after two months of marrige my husband starts quarreling & beating and doubting me of having an affier,even one day he tried to kill me by choking me, after that I went to my mother's house. On this he starts to say in all my nearby realatives and surrounding that he has divorced me, now we are not together, we are now seprated, reapetedly even when my brother went to him to discuss he said that he dont want to discuss any thing & he has given TALAQ to me, Then after some time he filed a case to call me back in court , but he himself not attended any hiearing and never shows any interest in solving the matter. That case got dissmissed by court. Now he has filled a case aginest me for divorce and is asking for rs 300000 for out of court divorce and is refusing to pay my meher, now it has passed abot 1.5 yrs my family is getting impatient whether i am married or divorced , should i start my period of iddah, or shuld i get ready for this out of court settelment by paying rs 300000 & geting divorce paper signed. now he only talkes on phone & it comes to my knowledge from some relible source of his side(with photograph of marrige) that he has married some other girl in delhi & told her parents that he has divorced me . Kindly Guide me shuld i consider his declairing in public as divorce & ask for meher, or shuld i consider my self married. 2046 views Q. The shariat rules of giving tala1 2155 views Q. Can you please get clarified my following masla from Mufi sahib. I have been married for 2 years. For the last two months there has been quarrel with my wife on very small issues. Actually, my parents stay in a village and I stay with my wife in a city where I do job. We generally visit my parent 2-3 times in a year for 5-7 days. Recently, when we were at my parent place on a small issue my wife told -"Mujku thumharey maa baap ki zarorat nahi". I got anger and replied -"phir mujku bhi teri zaroorat nahi.". This happens two times. After that I left her at her parents' place. Presently, now and then on phone we start fighting and in anger I used to tell words like -" Hum doono ko nahi ban rah hai", "tho jaa"..etc. I never uttered any word like "talaq". I have following 4 questions- 1. Will the words I told to my wife going to impact my Nikha? 2.Sometimes it comes to my mind to give talaq to my wife, but actually I do not want. And there is always something like wasawasa in my mind that I told talaq in my mind, but I never uttered any word from my mouth even when I was alone. Will this effect my nikha? 3. When somebody spells "talaaq" to wife in her absence, ie no one is around, Is talaq still valid? 4. What should be the minimum sound needed to utter "talaq", so that talaq is valid? 2810 views Q. Annulment of marriage 7605 views Q. Claim for Talaq 1806 views Q. One of my friends is in a state of confusion regarding HAQ-e-Mahar. 3 years back he has done his NIKAH with a girl in his relation and he went to abroad for his studies. There was no RUKSATI and the girl was still living at her home. In the mean time the girl lost interest in my friend and she gave the reason that he is very conservative and religious. She was asking again and again for Talaq. In spite of a lot of negotiations from both families this relation was failed and finally last week my friend gave her Talaq on phone and in written. Now the question is, as I stated before there was no RUKSATI took place. Only NIKAH was done. The girl is un-touched. So, the boy have to pay HAQ-e-Mahar or not? 1842 views
answer: Social Matters >> Talaq (Divorce) Question ID: 48779 Country: India Title: According to Sunni-Hanafi Teachings- Talaaq Procedure- Will Nikah remains if Talaaq is pronounced 3 times at a time according to sunni-hanafi teaching Question: I got married and had a 2 years old daughter. After marriage I come to know about the affairs of my wife. But I warned and excused her many times. Recently I come to about her new affair. So I prepared myself completely and gave talaq to her by visiting Qazaat Office and completed total procedure guided by Qazi and Pronounced "Talaaq, Talaaq, Talaaq" in front of Qazi and 2 witnesses. I prepared a notice and Sent to my wife's house along with the DD's of mahr amount and iddah period amount, but "she did not took it". I also took divorce certificate from Wakf Board, Hyderabad, India. Is my nikah valid or not? Now I want to accept (ruju) my wife because of my 2 years daughter. What is the procedure of re-accepting my wife? I heard that if we pronounce talaq for 3 times or number of times at a time, it will be treated as 1 talaq only. Is this correct according to sunni-Hanafi teachings? Answer ID: 48779 Posted on: Sep 1, 2020 Bismillah hir-Rahman nir-Rahim ! (Fatwa: 1373/1053/D=11/1434) In the above mentioned case three talaqs took place on the wife and their nikah came to an end completely. Now it is not lawful to marry her without a Shariah halalah, rather it is haram. قال فى العالمكيرى وان كان الطلاق ثلاثا فى الحرة .....لم تحل له حتى تنكح زوجاً غيره نكاحاً صحيحاً ويدخل بها ام يطلقها او يموث عنها كذا فى الهداية (هندیه ج 1 ص 473) Three talaqs occurs as three in any case whether given in single meeting or in different meetings three talaqs. The husband cannot marry her without a Shariah halalah. It is mentioned in the holy Quran and Hadith in clearly. The Sahabah have a consensus opinion about it as well the tabiyeen, tabe-tabiyeen, the four mujtahid Imams and all the Muhaddithin have the same opinion. The person who says that only one talaq took place he is a deviated person. You should study the book عمدة الاثاث فى الطلقات الثلاث or read Fatawa Rahimia, Ahsanul Fatawa in Urdu. You would find detailed and complete fatwa there. You may also find the detailed fatwa in the book named “Chand Aham Asari Masail”, a compilation of Fatawas issued by Darul Ifta and published by Maktaba Darul Uloom Deoband. Allah (Subhana Wa Ta'ala) knows Best Darul Ifta, Darul Uloom Deoband, India
